mechanic: An unreliable narrator: part of the story is told by someone whose statements can be doubted one by one. One of them is against what the other narrator knows himself; it is set aside, and another statement of the same narrator is kept.
note: Spoilers. The logic written before the prose, in the shape sketched in docs/archipelago-plan.md. The two narrators' parts are the clues. The first narrator is reliable (his own observations are certain and cannot be doubted singly); the second is marked `doubtable` in world/case.json.

frame.says: On Friday morning the strongroom was found open and four hundred pounds gone; the night porter wrote down his night.

questions.asks: Who took the four hundred pounds?

rules_out.Tobias Finch: c.lockup contradicts c.kemp_finch: he was locked up all night
rules_out.anyone without the keys: c.doors: nothing was forced; c.kemp_keys: the keys never left the porter

clues.says: He came on at ten; the keys of the bank and the strongroom never left his belt until the morning.
At one he saw the dismissed clerk looking in at the bank's window.
Neither the street door nor the strongroom door was forced: both were opened with their keys.
The dismissed clerk was in the Inspector's lock-up from ten on Thursday night until seven on Friday, the Inspector turning the key himself.
